body.x: Older adults who find smartphones difficult to operate are often left out of digital health services, and the services that do reach them still have to connect to the clinical systems used by hospitals and care facilities.
A companion that works by voice alone, reads a user's emotional state on the device itself and still feeds the records clinical staff rely on would address both problems.

AiMA, a digital health company founded in 2023 in Barcelona, Spain, and led by CEO Alex Izquierdo, has built its service around that idea. It offers a subscription-based digital health companion for older adults and patients with chronic conditions, and a multidisciplinary team of medical and clinical, marketing, software development and AI specialists runs the service alongside the CEO.

AiMA's core technology is an edge-computing architecture that combines voice and vision recognition with on-device emotional AI. The system analyzes a user's emotional and cognitive state on the device itself, which allows real-time responses while supporting data privacy and fast response times. It is designed to connect with the existing clinical systems of hospitals and care facilities through the international HL7/FHIR standard.

Users operate the service through a natural voice interface alone, so older adults who struggle with smartphones need no complex app navigation. Through proactive interventions such as medication reminders, AiMA aims to improve treatment adherence and reduce the burden on caregivers. The service supports English and Spanish, and it also supports Korean.

At KES 2026, AiMA is presenting the platform itself. Its booth runs a live demonstration of voice interaction, vision-based emotional and cognitive state recognition and on-device emotional AI, together with an HL7/FHIR-integrated dashboard designed for clinical staff. The company says the combination of voice-only access and clinical integration is its main differentiator.

AiMA currently works with the Spanish healthcare and welfare organization Althaia and with the elderly residences Lantus Group and Pere Mata. It has exhibited at the World Health Expo 2026 in Osaka, the Digital Public Health Conference 2026, SEGG 2026 (Spanish Society of Geriatrics and Gerontology) and KIMES 2026, and it plans to exhibit at MEDICA 2026 in Düsseldorf, Germany, and MWC Barcelona 2027.

AiMA has no export track record yet and has not generated overseas revenue. The company names Korea its priority market, citing rapid population ageing, strong policy interest in digital healthcare and a relatively high level of IT infrastructure in hospitals and care institutions. It is supported in its market search through the EU Business Hub program.

At KES, AiMA aims to establish an initial foothold in Korea by connecting with care institutions, hospitals and insurers and by learning about Korea's healthcare regulatory and certification environment. It is looking for two types of partner: local distribution or systems-integration partners that can deploy the service directly in care facilities and hospitals, and local partners experienced with Korean certification and medical-device regulatory processes. The company prioritizes partners that can support local operations and training, not only sales. At home, it plans to expand pilots with Althaia, Lantus Group and Pere Mata.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Approximately 50 European companies in the EU Business Hub program are showing digital solutions at the EU Pavilion, where participation is free and interpretation is provided, and B2B matchmaking with Korean companies is arranged in advance. The show's Digital Health & Lifestyle sector covers AI-powered healthcare, smart medical devices and senior and wellness technologies.
